verdict.rationale: ROS 2's built-in security layer (DDS-Security via sros2) supports authentication of participants, encrypted communications, and security 'enclaves' that encapsulate a policy for protecting communications, which can be used to restrict which nodes may command/configure/view topics or services — this is the closest analog to role-based access control. However, this is a low-level, per-node/participant policy mechanism configured via keystores and XML governance files, not a turnkey ops-facing UI or user/role management system for granting people specific command/configure/view permissions on robots. Missing for 10: evidence of a user-facing role/permission management interface, mapping of human operators to permission levels, and any hands-on/independent confirmation that this access-control system works as intended in production.
